questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: An 8-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with active bleeding from his left nostril after picking his nose. The bleeding is easily controlled with direct anterior digital compression. From which highly vascular anatomical site on the anterior septum did this epistaxis most likely originate?
questions.explanation: Little's area/Kiesselbach's plexus: anterior inferior nasal septum — confluence of 4 arteries (branches of anterior ethmoidal, sphenopalatine, superior labial, greater palatine). 90% of nosebleeds.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: A 36-year-old male with a history of severe granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener's) presents for evaluation of a progressive facial change. On examination, there is a prominent structural collapse of the middle third of the nasal dorsum. Destruction of which structural framework is responsible for this saddle nose deformity?

options.B: Destruction of the nasal septal cartilage and bony support
options.C: Atrophy of the soft tissue rhinophyma complex
options.D: Fibrosis of the ethmoid sinus osteomeatal unit

questions.explanation: Saddle nose: collapse of dorsum from cartilage/bone destruction. Causes: tertiary syphilis (classic), Wegener's GPA, relapsing polychondritis, trauma, cocaine abuse.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: A 27-year-old female presents with persistent clear rhinorrhea, sneezing bursts, and bilateral nasal congestion every spring. Physical examination shows pale, bluish, boggy inferior turbinates and a transverse skin crease across her nasal bridge. What is the fundamental immunological mechanism driving this presentation?
questions.explanation: Allergic rhinitis is driven by a Type I IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction against inhaled allergens. Signs include pale, boggy nasal mucosa, allergic shiners, and an 'allergic salute' crease on the nose.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: A 48-year-old male with a known history of aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (Samter's triad) complains of progressive bilateral nasal obstruction and anosmia. Anterior rhinoscopy reveals multiple smooth, translucent, grape-like masses insensitive to touch that originate from the ethmoid sinuses. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Ethmoidal polyps are multiple, bilateral, painless, translucent masses seen commonly in adults, often associated with allergies, asthma, and aspirin sensitivity (Samter's triad). Antrochoanal polyps are typically single, unilateral, and arise from the maxillary sinus.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: A 14-year-old boy presents with severe, unprovoked, recurrent unilateral posterior epistaxis and progressive left-sided nasal obstruction. Rhinology examination reveals a large, lobulated, highly vascular expansile mass filling the posterior nasal cavity. Contrast CT shows widening of the pterygopalatine fossa with anterior displacement of the posterior maxillary sinus wall (Holman-Miller sign). What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.C: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nasopharynx

questions.explanation: Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma (JNA) is a benign but locally aggressive, highly vascular tumor that occurs almost exclusively in adolescent males. It presents with the classic dyad of recurrent profuse epistaxis and unilateral nasal obstruction. The pathognomonic radiological sign is the Holman-Miller sign (anterior bowing of the posterior wall of the maxillary antrum).
